title: Isma'il, Idris, Dhul-Kifl: each of them was patient.
subtitle: Three names joined by one quality
then: Isma'il was the son of Ibrahim, and Idris was mentioned in Surah Maryam. Of Dhul-Kifl, the tafsir says {idea}the context suggests he was a prophet{/idea}; others said he was a righteous man and a just judge, and Ibn Jarir made no firm comment. {reward}What the verse records about all three is patience.{/reward}
now: Few people will know your name in a hundred years. Your job title won't matter. {idea}What lasts is a word like patient{/idea}: the parent who stayed calm, the carer who kept going. {reward}That is a legacy.{/reward}
old: To be remembered, I need to do something big.
new: Allah remembered these prophets with one word: patient. That can be my legacy too.
try: Choose one situation today where you will be patient on purpose.

title: Admitted into His mercy, for they were righteous.
subtitle: Where patience leads
then: Right after naming Isma'il, Idris and Dhul-Kifl as patient, Allah says {reward}We admitted them to Our mercy{/reward}. {idea}They were of the righteous.{/idea} The same words were said of Lut a few verses earlier.
now: You hold your tongue through the in-law's comments for the hundredth time. {trap}It feels like it goes nowhere.{/trap} {reward}Patience that is for Allah ends inside His mercy.{/reward}
old: Being patient just means putting up with things.
new: Patience for Allah's sake is a road into His mercy.
try: When you hold back a sharp word today, quietly ask Allah to count it for you.

title: In three darknesses, Yunus said: none but You, I was wrong.
subtitle: The prayer from inside the whale

key.label: What he did in the dark

then: Yunus {trap}left his people in anger{/trap} and boarded a ship; the lot fell on him and he was swallowed by a great fish. Ibn Mas'ud said the darknesses were {trap}the belly of the fish, the sea, and the night{/trap}. There he called: {idea}there is no god but You, glory be to You, I was of the wrongdoers{/idea}.
now: Stuck in the dark: the debt you can't see out of, the 3 a.m. panic, the mistake that cost you. {idea}Yunus didn't argue or blame.{/idea} He glorified Allah and owned his part. {reward}That prayer works from any darkness.{/reward}
old: When I am in a hole, the first thing is to work out who caused it.
new: In the dark, I turn to Allah, praise Him, and own my part.
try: Say the dua of Yunus three times today: La ilaha illa Anta, subhanaka, inni kuntu minaz-zalimin.

title: We answered him and saved him. So We save the believers.
subtitle: A promise that reaches past Yunus to you
then: Allah {reward}brought him out of the fish and the darkness{/reward}. The tafsir says {idea}this is how He saves believers{/idea} who call on Him in difficulty and repent, especially with these words. Sa'd reported the Prophet ﷺ said that no Muslim prays with them for anything except that He answers.
now: You think the story of Yunus is about a prophet, a whale, a long time ago. {idea}The last line is about you.{/idea} {reward}The same rescue is promised to anyone who calls the same way.{/reward}
old: Miracles of rescue happened to prophets, not to people like me.
new: Allah says He saves believers the way He saved Yunus. That promise includes me.
try: Make the dua of Yunus for one specific difficulty you are in right now.

title: Zakariyya prayed: do not leave me alone; You are the best heir.
subtitle: A quiet dua with praise woven in
then: Zakariyya {idea}cried to his Lord in secret, hiding it from his people{/idea}. He asked not to be left with no heir to stand among the people after him. The tafsir calls his closing words, {reward}You are the best of inheritors{/reward}, a praise befitting the request.
now: You want a child, or a spouse, or someone to carry on your work, and you feel embarrassed to keep asking. {idea}Zakariyya asked quietly, in old age{/idea}, and praised Allah with a name that fit his need.
old: Some wishes are too late or too private to keep asking for.
new: I can ask quietly, at any age, and praise Allah with the name that fits my need.
try: Make a private dua tonight, and end it with a name of Allah that fits what you asked.

title: They rushed to good, called in hope and fear, and were humble.
subtitle: The family whose dua was answered with Yahya
then: Allah gave Zakariyya Yahya and {reward}cured his wife{/reward}, who had been barren. Then He describes them: they {idea}hastened to good deeds{/idea}, called on Him in hope and fear, and were humble. Abu Sinan said khushu' is {idea}the fear that should never leave our hearts{/idea}.
now: You plan to start the good deed when things calm down: the volunteering, the extra prayer, the visit to your aunt. {trap}They never calm down.{/trap} {idea}The ones Allah praised rushed to good.{/idea}
old: I will do more good when I have more time.
new: The people Allah praised rushed to good, with hope and fear and humility.
try: Do the good deed you have been postponing today, even in a small form.

title: Maryam guarded her chastity; she and her son became a sign.
subtitle: A wonder even greater than Zakariyya's
then: Zakariyya's story, a child to an old man and barren wife, comes first because the two are connected. Then comes Maryam's, {idea}even more wondrous{/idea}: a child born without a father. The tafsir says she and her son are {reward}evidence that Allah is able to do all things{/reward}.
now: Doctors gave you the odds. The bank said no. Your situation looks closed by every normal rule. {idea}Allah's power is not bound by the odds.{/idea} {reward}Keep your own purity, and leave the impossible to Him.{/reward}
old: Some outcomes are simply impossible in my situation.
new: Allah creates what He wills. My part is to stay upright, like Maryam.
try: Make one dua today for something you had written off as impossible.

title: Your religion is one religion, and I am your Lord.
subtitle: All the prophets just named stood on one path
then: After the long list of prophets, Allah says: {idea}your religion is one religion{/idea}. The Prophet ﷺ said {reward}we prophets are brothers from different mothers, and our religion is one{/reward}. They all worshipped Allah alone, though their laws differed.
now: You read about Nuh, Ibrahim, Musa, Yunus, Maryam, 'Isa. {idea}They are not distant strangers. They are your spiritual family{/idea}, all calling to the same Lord you pray to. {reward}You belong to a long line.{/reward}
old: The prophets of the past belong to different stories.
new: All the prophets brought one religion. I stand in their line when I worship Allah.
try: Read the story of one prophet from this surah again and notice what you share.

title: People split apart, but every one of them returns to Us.
subtitle: Division on earth, one return to Allah
then: The nations {trap}were divided over their messengers{/trap}: some believed and some rejected. Allah says {idea}they all shall return to Us{/idea}. On the Day of Resurrection, the tafsir says, each person will be repaid according to his own deeds.
now: The family WhatsApp group splits over an argument. The mosque committee divides. {trap}You spend energy proving you're right.{/trap} {idea}Everyone is heading to the same return, where your own deeds are what count.{/idea}
old: Settling who is right in every dispute matters most.
new: We all return to Allah. My own deeds matter more than winning the argument.
try: Step out of one argument today and spend that energy on a good deed.

title: Good done with faith is never rejected. We write it down.
subtitle: No sincere effort is wasted
then: Whoever does good while believing, {idea}his heart believes and his deeds are righteous{/idea}, the tafsir says. {reward}His efforts will not be wasted{/reward}; they will be appreciated, without a speck of injustice. All his deeds are recorded, and nothing is lost.
now: The night feeds no one thanked you for. The report your boss took credit for. The care for a parent who no longer recognises you. {trap}It feels invisible.{/trap} {reward}It is written down.{/reward}
old: If nobody notices what I do, it doesn't really count.
new: Every good I do with faith is recorded. None of it is lost.
try: Do one unseen good deed today and tell no one.

title: A destroyed town will not come back for a second chance.
subtitle: This life is the only time to act
then: Ibn 'Abbas said the ban is enforced: {trap}it has been decreed that the people of each destroyed town will never return to this world{/trap} before the Day of Resurrection. {idea}There is no going back to fix it.{/idea}
now: Games have restart buttons. Phones have undo. {trap}Life does not.{/trap} {idea}This day, this family, this chance to make things right, is the one you get.{/idea}
old: There will always be another chance to get it right.
new: No one comes back to redo their life. Today is the chance.
try: Do one thing today you would want done if you had no tomorrow.

title: Until Ya'juj and Ma'juj are let loose, rushing from every height.
subtitle: A sign of the end, told by the One who knows
then: The tafsir says they will {trap}come forth quickly to spread corruption{/trap}, rushing down from every raised piece of land, described {idea}as if the listener can see it{/idea}. This is information from the One who knows what has happened and what is to come.
now: Endless videos online claim to decode the end times. {trap}It is easy to get lost in speculation.{/trap} {idea}What Allah tells you about the end is a reminder to get ready, not a puzzle.{/idea}
old: Knowing the signs of the end is about predicting when.
new: The signs are told so I prepare, not so I speculate.
try: Skip one end-times video today and spend those minutes in dhikr.

title: The true promise arrives: we were heedless, we were wrong.
subtitle: The same confession the surah opened with
then: The surah began: {trap}the reckoning is near, yet they are heedless{/trap}. Here the deniers say it themselves: woe to us, we were heedless of this. Then they correct themselves: {idea}no, we were wrongdoers{/idea}. Heedlessness had been a choice.
now: You tell yourself you are just busy, just distracted, not bad. {trap}Busy can be a polite word for choosing not to look.{/trap} {idea}The verse asks you to name it now, while it can still change.{/idea}
old: I am not doing wrong, I am just busy and distracted.
new: Staying heedless is a choice. I would rather notice now than say it then.
try: Name one thing you've been too busy for that matters to Allah. Give it ten minutes today.

title: You and what you worship besides Allah fuel the Fire.
subtitle: False gods end up where their worshippers do
then: Allah addressed the idolaters of Quraysh: {trap}you and what you worship besides Allah are fuel for Hell{/trap}. Ibn 'Abbas said the word means kindling. Ibn Ishaq reported the Prophet ﷺ recited this in the Masjid after {idea}defeating An-Nadr bin Al-Harith in argument{/idea}.
now: Whatever you make the centre of your life in place of Allah: money, status, a person's approval. {trap}It cannot save you; it will not even save itself.{/trap} {idea}Put Allah back in the centre while you can.{/idea}
old: What I put at the centre of my life will look after me.
new: Anything I worship besides Allah will fail with me. Only He can save.
try: Ask: what do I fear losing more than Allah's pleasure? Make dua to put it in its place.
